name: hcapp_joinEventAsVisitor
description: Records a non-member attendee (virgin = 1, visitor = 2) against an event. Uses a per-kennel placeholder Hasher whose id equals the KennelId; this row is created on demand if it does not already exist. The HasherEventMap row is idempotent by DisplayName: if a row already exists for that display name and event it is reused and the caller receives the existing hasherEventMapId without updating any fields. On success delegates to HC6.hcapp_syncEventAdminData to return fresh event admin sync data. Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 23, @param NULL). No permission gate of its own: any authenticated user may add a visitor to any visible event (the delegated sync re-validates auth for its own rowsets).

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Passed to HC6.ValidateAppAuth.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived cryptographic token validated by HC6.ValidateAppAuth.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Event UUID to add the visitor to. Must not be null or the zero UUID.

parameters.name: displayName
parameters.description: Visitor's display name. Used for deduplication — if a HEM row with this DisplayName already exists for the event, the existing row is returned unchanged.
parameters.typeMismatch: Parameter is NVARCHAR(250); HasherEventMap.DisplayName is NVARCHAR(120). Values longer than 120 characters will cause a string truncation error at insert time.

parameters.name: virginVisitorType
parameters.description: 1 = Virgin, 2 = Visitor. Any other value returns an explicit errorType=12 param error (breaking change vs HC5 which silently did nothing).

parameters.name: attendenceState
parameters.description: Initial attendance state to set on the new HEM row (e.g. 20 = on trail). Not applied when the idempotent path reuses an existing row.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Visitor's email address; NULL allowed by the body but the parameter has NO SQL default, so it must be passed. Not applied when the idempotent path reuses an existing row.
parameters.typeMismatch: Parameter is NVARCHAR(250); HasherEventMap.Email is NVARCHAR(120). Values longer than 120 characters will cause a string truncation error at insert time.

parameters.name: phoneNumber
parameters.description: Visitor's phone number; NULL allowed by the body but the parameter has NO SQL default, so it must be passed. Not applied when the idempotent path reuses an existing row.
parameters.typeMismatch: Parameter is NVARCHAR(250); HasherEventMap.PhoneNumber is NVARCHAR(120). Values longer than 120 characters will cause a string truncation error at insert time.

parameters.name: hasherEventMapUpdatedAfter
parameters.description: Sync watermark forwarded to HC6.hcapp_syncEventAdminData; NULL is coerced to 'ignore' (line 213) — but the parameter has NO SQL default, so it must be passed.

parameters.name: paymentsUpdatedAfter
parameters.description: Sync watermark forwarded to HC6.hcapp_syncEventAdminData; NULL is coerced to 'ignore' (line 214) — but the parameter has NO SQL default, so it must be passed.

rowsets.name: Envelope
rowsets.description: Write SP success envelope. Always the first rowset: { 0, errorCode, errorType } on auth failure (ValidateAppAuth), missing eventId (1223/12), bad virginVisitorType (1223/12) or the CATCH block (1923/19); { 1, NULL, NULL } on success.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: NULL on success. Error code on failure.

columns.name: errorType
columns.description: NULL on success. Error classification on failure. 11=auth, 12=param, 19=db.

rowsets.name: ErrorDetail
rowsets.description: Returned only on error (when envelope success=0). Contains one row with error detail.

columns.name: errorId
columns.description: UUID of the HC.ErrorLog entry written for this error.

columns.name: errorProc
columns.description: Name of the SP that raised the error, from OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID).

rowsets.name: AdHocResult
rowsets.description: Returned only on success (when envelope success=1). Single row identifying the new or existing HEM record.

columns.name: hasherEventMapId
columns.description: The newly created or pre-existing HasherEventMap.id for this visitor.

rowsets.name: SyncEventAdminData
rowsets.description: On success, all subsequent rowsets come from HC6.hcapp_syncEventAdminData executed outside the transaction after the commit. The shape of these rowsets is defined by that SP's contract.

sideEffects: INSERT HC.Hasher — placeholder Hasher row (id = KennelId) created on demand if none exists for the event's kennel; triggers on HC.Hasher (QR code generation, geolocation, etc.) will fire
INSERT HC.HasherEventMap — new visitor row created if no existing row with the same DisplayName for this event; skipped on the idempotent path
EXEC HC6.hcapp_syncEventAdminData — called after the transaction commits to return fresh sync data; auth is re-validated inside the delegated SP
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on 1223 (lines 92-94, 105-107, before the transaction) and from the CATCH block (lines 200-201, after ROLLBACK)

codeSmells.detail: All ten parameters (lines 3-12) have no SQL default. A client that omits any of them — including the optional @email / @phoneNumber and the two watermarks the body COALESCEs to 'ignore' at lines 213-214 — gets 'expects parameter': an unlogged empty 500 before the SP runs, so the graceful 1223 checks at lines 89 and 102 are unreachable for an omitted parameter. The four that tolerate NULL should default to it.

codeSmells.issue: Parameter type wider than column for DisplayName, Email, PhoneNumber
codeSmells.detail: @displayName, @email, and @phoneNumber are all declared NVARCHAR(250), but the corresponding columns HasherEventMap.DisplayName, Email, and PhoneNumber are each NVARCHAR(120). Any value longer than 120 characters will silently truncate or raise an error at INSERT time depending on ANSI_WARNINGS settings. Should be narrowed to NVARCHAR(120) to match the table.
Lines 119-123 declare and populate @kennelId from the event, but nothing reads it — the two INSERTs re-derive e.KennelId themselves. Dead code.

codeSmells.issue: DisplayName de-duplication ignores removed rows and the visitor type
codeSmells.detail: Lines 153-157 reuse ANY HasherEventMap row of the event with the same DisplayName — including a removed one, or a registered hasher's row whose DisplayName happens to match — so a visitor can be silently attached to the wrong row. VirginVisitorType and removed are not in the predicate.

codeSmells.issue: Idempotent path does not update existing row
codeSmells.detail: When a HasherEventMap row already exists for the given DisplayName and EventId, the SP returns the existing hasherEventMapId without applying @attendenceState, @email, or @phoneNumber. If the caller is correcting a previously recorded state (e.g. changing attendance state from RSVP to on-trail), the update is silently dropped. This is a data staleness risk — callers have no way to know whether the returned row reflects current or prior values.

codeSmells.issue: Placeholder Hasher INSERT may fail due to missing required columns
codeSmells.detail: The INSERT at lines 132-147 names only nine columns and relies on table DEFAULT constraints for every other NOT NULL column of HC.Hasher (PublicHasherId, SupportCode, ResetCode, QR codes, Preferences, flags, timestamps). It works today; a new NOT NULL column without a default would break visitor sign-up for any kennel that has not yet got its placeholder.

codeSmells.issue: adHocDataId is a literal sentinel with no meaning
codeSmells.detail: The success rowset always returns adHocDataId = 1 as a hard-coded literal. This column carries no information — the caller only needs hasherEventMapId. The column exists for historical HC5 compatibility and should be considered for removal in a future cleanup.

codeSmells.issue: Duplicate errorCode 1223 used for two distinct param errors
codeSmells.detail: errorCode 1223 is used for both the null/zero @eventId check (line 91) and the invalid @virginVisitorType check (line 104). Callers cannot distinguish these two failure modes by errorCode alone — they must inspect errorTitle or errorUserMessage.

breakingChanges: Invalid @virginVisitorType now returns an explicit errorType=12 error rowset. HC5 silently returned no rowsets and made no changes for values other than 1 or 2.
TRY/CATCH and transaction added. HC5 had neither — an unhandled runtime error in HC5 would propagate to the caller without any error envelope.
Success envelope rowset (rowset 0) added. HC5 returned only the AdHocResult rowset on success with no envelope.
Delegation target changed from HC5.hcapp_syncEventAdminData to HC6.hcapp_syncEventAdminData.
